title: Coherent module pullback and derived tensor on ambient coefficient categories
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes; their structure maps are not required to be separated [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each $T$, choose either $\mathscr M_T=\operatorname{Mod}((A_n)_T)$ at one fixed $n$, or the category $\mathscr M_T$ of module sheaves $M_n$ over $(A_n)_T$ with semilinear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{n+1}\to A_n}M_n$ and compatible componentwise morphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathscr M_T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a scheme map $f$ write $f^*$ for exact constant-coefficient module inverse image and $P_f=D(f^*)$; for an open immersion $j$ write $j_!$ for exact extension by zero and $J_j=D(j_!)$. Use the specified adjunctions $P_f\dashv S_f=Rf_*$ and $J_j\dashv P_j$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. System operations are constructed simultaneously on the ringed diagram site, before finite evaluation, scalar restriction or total limit [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

For composable $u:X\to Y$, $v:Y\to Z$, let $\widetilde d_{v,u}:u^*v^*\cong(vu)^*$ be the adjunction-compatible comparison induced by the canonical fibre-product section comparison for direct images [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. With the canonical constant-ring maps $c_u:u^{-1}(A_n)_Y\cong(A_n)_X$, its local tensor formula is
$$ (m\otimes a)\otimes b\longmapsto m\otimes c_u(a)b. $$
This formula gives morphisms of semilinear systems, preserving all coefficient transitions. The constant-ring maps satisfy $c_{vu}=c_u\circ u^{-1}(c_v)\circ\alpha_{u,v}$, where $\alpha_{u,v}:(vu)^{-1}\cong u^{-1}v^{-1}$ is the canonical inverse-image comparison. The comparisons $\widetilde d$ preserve the composite adjunction units and are natural, associative and unital. Their exact localizations $d_{v,u}:P_uP_v\cong P_{vu}$ have the same laws.

Let $\mu_f:P_f(F\otimes^{\mathbf L}G)\cong P_fF\otimes^{\mathbf L}P_fG$ be the canonical derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The following equality of natural transformations holds in $D(\mathscr M_X)$:
$$ (d_{v,u,F}\otimes d_{v,u,G})\circ\mu_u\circ P_u(\mu_v)=\mu_{vu}\circ d_{v,u,F\otimes^{\mathbf L}G}. $$
The ordinary module tensor comparisons satisfy the corresponding equality on sheaf tensor products. For K-flat flat-term complexes representing $F,G$, their successive pullbacks are K-flat with flat terms, and the two chain maps on their total tensor complexes coincide and represent this derived equality [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. All associators are canonical. The system equality is an equality before evaluation, for arbitrary unbounded system inputs, without a cartesian-system or flat-transition hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules); sites.tex Tag 03CB (lemma-composition-morphisms-sites). Agent extension of the explicit tensor formula and K-flat comparison to both ambient coefficient settings; returned proof Steps 1 and 3.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition] with $h=u,k=v,A=A_n$: this is exactly the asserted equation for $c_{vu}$, with the direction of $\alpha$ as written in the item. The canonical maps are also natural in $A_n\to A_r$: the two composites send every constant section $a$ to the same reduced constant section. The constant-sheaf sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] makes these ring-sheaf maps equal; [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] identifies them with the specified $c_f$. Thus these are compatible maps of ring towers. For systems use the ringed sequence site of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]; its ring restrictions are precisely the quotient maps. The underlying geometric inverse image on sequence topoi is levelwise $f^{-1}$: the levelwise topos adjunction restricts to compatible families of maps by naturality of its hom bijection, and finite limits are componentwise. Together with the preceding ring-tower maps this is a morphism of ringed topoi. Its module inverse image is the exact system functor of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. This supplies a single ringed-site setting for the rest of the proof, not an inference of morphism equality from derived evaluations. In the Lean implementation, finite exactness uses [lem-pur-coefficient-pullback-exact]. For systems apply [lem-sf-sequence-module-pullback-evaluation] to the sectionwise identity direct-image comparison; its inverse mate identifies ordinary pullback at each level. Componentwise exactness from [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] then proves exactness of the simultaneous module pullback.

source.place: Tags 03CB (lemma-composition-morphisms-sites, sites.tex) and 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules); constant-sheaf and sequence-site specialization

proof.text: At each level apply [lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit] with $h=u,k=v,R_T=(A_n)_T$ and Step 1's coefficient equation. It gives the natural invertible map $(m\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto m\otimes c_u(a)b$, its inverse $m\otimes b\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes b$, and its composite-adjunction unit equation for precisely the direct-image section comparison in the item. These are also system morphisms. Indeed, if $\theta:M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}M_n$ is any semilinear transition, either route around the transition square sends $((m\otimes a)\otimes b)$ to $\theta(m)\otimes c_{u,n}(\bar a)\bar b$, since $\overline{c_{u,n+1}(a)b}=c_{u,n}(\bar a)\bar b$. The inverse formula has the same property. This verifies every horizontal restriction as well as the vertical ones. Ordinary system morphisms and adjunction units are compatible componentwise maps by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; hence the displayed unit equations are equalities of system morphisms. This uses no condition on $\theta$ beyond semilinearity.

source.place: Tag 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules); explicit comparison and unit equation of lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit

proof.text: For a third scheme map $w:W\to X$, the two direct-image composition maps are equal: both identify the iterated fibre product over a site object with its single composite fibre product, preserving every projection, so [def-pc-fibre-product] gives equality. Apply [lem-trf-adjoint-composition-coherence] to these direct-image isomorphisms and the module adjunctions: its unit-compatible left-adjoint comparisons are Step 2's maps, so they are associative. The scalar check is $(((m\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes e)\mapsto m\otimes c_w(w^{-1}(c_u)(a))c_w(b)e$ along either route, using Step 1's equation. With an identity map the comparison is the scalar-action unitor $m\otimes b\mapsto mb$, inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Its unit equation is the identity-adjunction equation of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] identifies it with the specified identity comparison. Consequently the two unit laws follow by substitution in Step 2's formula. All these equations hold for ordinary systems because the maps have already been constructed there.

source.place: Tags 03CB (sites.tex) and 03D3; categories.tex Tags 0B65 and 0DV0; scalar associativity and identity

proof.text: The ordinary tensor comparison exists and is natural by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. In the right-scalar convention its normalized formula is $(x\otimes y)\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes1)$. Its inverse sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$; balancing verifies that both formulas are well defined and mutually inverse, so they give the canonical tensor comparison. For the inverse-image factor use [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison], whose composition equation identifies the iterated pullbacks of $x\otimes y$ with the tensor of the iterated pullbacks of $x$ and $y$. Now both routes in the ordinary tensor square in the statement send $((x\otimes y)\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $(x\otimes c_u(a)b)\otimes(y\otimes1)$. The inverse-image composition on $x,y$ is the same on both routes by that cited equation. Equality extends from these generators by the tensor/sheafification universal property [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This also holds for systems: at a transition each coefficient becomes its reduction and $x,y$ become $\theta_M(x),\theta_N(y)$, respectively. Step 1's ring-map naturality gives the same displayed answer after reduction on either route. Thus the tensor comparisons and the entire square are maps and an equality on the ringed sequence site itself. Arbitrary transitions are allowed; neither transition is being identified with a scalar-extension isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); canonical generator calculation for composite pullback

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] to the ringed topoi of Step 1, either the finite sites or the sequence sites. Its comparison on possibly unbounded complexes is the direct-sum total of the ordinary comparisons and it satisfies the composition equation with the canonical scalar-multiplication compositor, which Step 2 identified with $\widetilde d$. This is the displayed tensor square on complexes. More explicitly, in each summand of total degree $p+q$ its two maps are Step 4's equal maps. They preserve $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$ because the ordinary comparison is natural in both module arguments; no factor is permuted. Equality on every summand yields equality on the whole direct sum by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. In the system case these are chain maps of modules on the sequence site, so this equality precedes both localization and evaluation.

Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $P\to F$ and $Q\to G$ on this single ringed site by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. In the system case they resolve the entire systems, not separately chosen levels. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] successively to $v,u,vu$: the complexes $v^*P,v^*Q,u^*v^*P,u^*v^*Q,(vu)^*P,(vu)^*Q$ are all K-flat with flat terms, and their total tensors compute the required derived tensors. Exact pullback is computed termwise on every complex by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], so localization of the Step 2 compositor computes $d$, including on $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)$. The canonical derived tensor comparison is the localized total ordinary comparison of Step 5, as in the K-flat construction of Tag 07A4 and [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] for system operations. Therefore localizing Step 5 gives exactly $(d_F\otimes d_G)\mu_uP_u(\mu_v)=\mu_{vu}d_{F\otimes^LG}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], these natural transformations are determined on flat-term K-flat representatives; hence the equality holds naturally for all unbounded inputs.

Finally apply the natural-transformation localization property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the exact termwise pullbacks. It preserves composition, identities and natural isomorphisms, so Step 3's associativity, identity and naturality equations descend to $d$. This completes the exact-localization assertions in addition to the tensor square of Step 6. The chain-map comparison in Step 5 took place on the ringed sequence site and Step 6 resolved that site as a whole; thus the derived system equality is established there before evaluation. No faithfulness of evaluation on derived morphisms, flatness of coefficient transitions, or cartesian condition has entered.

source.place: categories.tex Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization); full faithfulness of restriction along localization

proof.text: For tensorData_existsUnique, apply the ordinary ringed-site pullback generator theorem to the finite site or the single ringed sequence site. Base change is representably flat, including its product with the natural-number identity. Totalize the resulting natural ordinary comparison and descend it with the flat-term K-flat representative models. Assemble the normalized ordinary, chain and derived data with an abstract exact functor first, then specialize to the selected ambient pullback. The ambient pure-section abbreviation shares the independent-size canonical sheafification construction, so generator normalization and naturality transport to the constructed bundle. Conversely the ordinary uniqueness theorem identifies any other ordinary part; uniqueness of total and derived TensorComparisonModel data identifies the entire bundle. The final ambientPullbackTensorCoherence proof remains an open named theorem with the preceding planned steps. The exactness verification compares the underlying section functors by a componentwise natural isomorphism and reflects their finite limits.
